title: Media Forge job request

operation.description: image.generate creates a new image. image.edit changes an existing image. video.generate creates video from text or bounded key images. video.edit changes existing video. asset.pack bundles existing assets.

intent.description: Plain description of the subject and the purpose, in any language. Structural requirements belong in constraints.asset_brief, not in adjectives here: a request that said 'wide landscape' only in this field was produced as a square.

inputs.description: Existing assets this job reads. image.edit needs exactly one, or 2..4 when constraints.edit_mode is 'multi_reference'. Give either an asset_id from a previous Media Forge result, or a grant_id for a file in the current Control Deck project.

model_policy.description: Leave as 'auto' unless the person asked for a specific tradeoff. 'quality' and 'low_vram' are for when the task genuinely needs them; 'manual' additionally requires model_id and is for explicit user model selection only.

constraints.description: Free-form generation constraints. Explicit integer width/height here always win over anything inferred, for image.generate and for the image.edit modes that redraw the whole picture. Prefer describing purpose in constraints.asset_brief and letting Media Forge resolve the geometry.

width.description: Exact output width. Overrides every inferred geometry rule.

height.description: Exact output height. Overrides every inferred geometry rule.

scene_texture.description: Durable 3D Studio return context for an image.generate job. It does not grant scene mutation authority; applying the resulting immutable image still requires MaterialBinding against the current revision.

edit_mode.description: How an image.edit job changes its inputs. 'reference' (the default) redraws the whole picture from one input image and the intent — use it to change pose, angle or wardrobe while keeping the same subject; it needs exactly one entry in inputs. 'multi_reference' does the same from 2..4 input images, so a front view and a side view can together produce a back view; it needs 2..4 entries in inputs. 'variation' redraws one input as an alternative take. The remaining modes are narrower: 'inpaint', 'outpaint' and 'masked_edit' work on a painted area, and 'upscale', 'deblur' and 'erase' are repairs whose output size comes from the model. Anything other than 'multi_reference' takes exactly one input. The whole-picture modes also honour constraints.asset_brief: a brief that requires transparency makes the edited result transparent, the same way generation does.

strict_edit.description: Keep the pixels outside the edited area unchanged. This is for touching up part of a picture, not for redrawing it: a pose or angle change needs the whole image redrawn, so leave this false there. 'inpaint' and 'outpaint' require it; 'variation' refuses it.

assetInput.description: One image this job reads. Give exactly one of the two: asset_id for something Media Forge already holds (an id returned by an earlier generate), or grant_id for a file in the current Control Deck project. Get a grant_id by calling the host's control_deck.project_input_grant tool with the file's path inside the project; Media Forge imports the file and uses it like any other asset.

count.description: How many images to produce from this one request. They are generated in the same call with the model kept loaded, each from a different seed, so asking for several takes far less time than repeating the call. Use it to get alternatives of the same idea and pick one; the spread between them is not steerable.

qa.description: Leave at the defaults for ordinary generation. semantic=true asks for a vision evaluation, which costs a model swap; max_regeneration_attempts bounds subjective retries only. Objective mismatches against the brief are always corrected or reported regardless of this budget.

assetBrief.title: What the asset is for
assetBrief.description: Purpose-level description. Media Forge resolves the canvas, aspect ratio and transparency from this deterministically, before generation, so a landscape requirement cannot silently come back square. Everything is optional; give what the consuming code actually requires.

role.description: Where the asset is used. This sets the default aspect ratio and whether transparency is required: 'emblem' and 'sprite' are drawn over something else and default to requiring alpha; 'background' fills a surface and defaults to landscape and opaque.

target_surface.description: Where it will be shown, when known: web, game, m5, print.

composition_intent.description: How the subject should sit in the frame.

aspect_intent.description: Use 'ratio' together with aspect_ratio for an exact ratio.

aspect_ratio.description: Exact ratio such as '16:9'. Read the consuming layout rather than guessing.

safe_areas.description: Regions to keep visually clear for something else, such as a title or HUD. Composition intent, not a pixel-level guarantee.

alpha_intent.description: Set 'required' whenever the asset is drawn over something else. An overlay generated without transparency arrives as an opaque rectangle with visible edges. When this is 'required', say nothing about the background in intent: Media Forge generates the subject on a flat chroma background of its own and removes it deterministically after generation. Asking for a background here contradicts that instruction and leaves an opaque halo around the subject. Media Forge cuts the subject out itself; you may describe whatever background you want and it is honoured.

consistency_group.description: Share one name across sibling assets that must look like a set.

hard_constraints.description: Requirements that must not be traded away, such as 'no text in the image'.

description:
Ask for what the asset is FOR. Media Forge resolves the canvas, the prompt wording for whichever model is routed, and the model itself. Do not write provider-tuned prompts and do not name a model: an agent that knows one model's preferred phrasing produces worse output the day the routing changes.

Need more than one asset? Use media.generate.batch instead of calling this repeatedly. Every separate call makes the host unload and reload the language model around the generation; one batch call keeps the image model loaded for the whole run. For several variants of the SAME idea, output.count is enough.

Transparency and geometry are resolved from constraints.asset_brief, not from the wording of intent. A sprite or emblem asked for in prose alone comes back opaque and square: set asset_brief.role ('sprite' and 'emblem' default to requiring alpha, 'background' to landscape and opaque).

examples.intent: Night riverside fireworks festival for a game title screen
A single golden chrysanthemum firework as a title emblem
